title: Cinnamon and Raisin Puff Pastry Waffle
changes_from_base: No batter at all: puff pastry spread with a strip of cream cheese, scattered with raisins, cinnamon and sugar, rolled into a spiral and cooked in the waffle iron to 93 °C.
summary: Puff pastry rolled with cream cheese, raisins and cinnamon, coiled into a spiral and cooked in the waffle iron until golden.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust the work surface and the 225 g sheet of thawed puff pastry with flour, then roll it into a square about 40 x 40 cm.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Spread 115 g cream cheese in an even strip across the centre, leaving 2.5 cm clear at both ends.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Scatter 35 g raisins over the pastry, leaving a 2.5 cm border, then dust lightly with cinnamon and sprinkle with caster sugar.

steps.title: Coil
steps.text: Roll the pastry away from you like a Swiss roll, pinch the seam and ends to seal, then coil it into a flat spiral.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place in the centre of the hot iron and cook until deep golden brown all over and a thermometer reads 93 °C in the centre, about 10 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut into wedges on a board and serve at once.

tips: Leave the clear borders as given so the filling stays sealed inside as it cooks.
A light dusting of cinnamon and sugar before rolling spreads the flavour evenly through every layer of the spiral.
Use the thermometer to confirm the centre has reached 93 °C, since the coiled layers take longer to heat through than a flat waffle.
storage: Best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the iron. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
